points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the existing candidate record and were not re-adjudicated.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English Google result pages. Page one mixes a Medium comparison, release notes, an independent integration overview, Spectacles product and GitHub pages, Looker CI configuration docs, a forum announcement, and generic Looker migration articles; page two falls into unrelated BI migrations, old Spectacles usage, vendor pages, and general Looker CI usage.

G2=pass: inner documentation, independent blogs, product pages, forums, and generic migration content share the SERP; there is no video, wiki, major-media, or strong-brand-homepage takeover, and page two shows an exact-task quality cliff.

The Looker Admin Continuous Integration page fully configures native CI—enablement, CI users, access grants, GitHub app permissions, repository access, and pull-request triggering—but does not map or remove an existing legacy Spectacles service configuration.

The first natural Medium article explicitly states that it is not a how-to. It compares validator parity, triggers, notifications, content management, and migration risks, but directs setup to the official CI documentation. The Rittman Analytics result explains the product integration rather than executing a legacy-service migration.

G3=pass: no free result completes the end-to-end legacy Spectacles service to native Looker CI migration across the first two pages; configuration, comparison, and announcement pages are complementary but not exact-task completions.
This is not veto_window_bet because no already-built exact migration implementations were found merely awaiting indexing.

Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The legacy standalone service has a dated November 30, 2026 discontinuation, while native CI configuration and comparison material are already mature enough for a migration guide to emerge quickly.

Invalidation conditions: two free end-to-end Spectacles-to-Looker-CI migration guides become stably visible; Google publishes an official migration checklist that maps suites, validators, triggers, notifications, and service teardown; the November 30, 2026 discontinuation date or Looker CI parity changes.
Caveat: Chrome used a signed-in Google session with gl=us, hl=en, pws=0; the result footer reported that results were not personalized, while safe=active and ssui=on were appended by Google.
